newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude gains on short covering, strike threat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude gains on short covering, strike threat.

text.p: NYMEX crude sharpened its gains Tuesday afternoon on news petroleum industry workers in Nigeria threatened to go on strike, although much of crude's rise was due to short covering, traders said.
"The Nigerian news may have added 10 to 15 cents to the crude, but this is really a short covering rally ahead of the APIs," said a New York crude dealer.

At 1444 EST, March crude was up 55 cents at $21.26 a barrel. The American Petroleum Institute was expected to report weekly oil inventory data Tuesday evening, and traders wanted to square positions in case the data held surprises.

Workers of the Department of Petroleum Resources (DPR) which processes export documents for oil shipments have threatened to go on strike from Friday if the backlog of their salaries are not paid, oil ministry sources said on Tuesday.
Dealers downplayed the significance of the possible strike on the market, saying the workers were not responsible for production, so there was no imminent threat to supply.
"We talked about it for about 13.5 seconds," said one dealer of the news.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
